notes:
Summary: Orion Guard runs real-time threat detection + analyst-assist across 2,000 enterprise customers. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and cross-region failover. Preference: reserved GPU pools (H100-equivalent) with explicit headroom for incident spikes and AZ failover.

Key requirements / numbers (from capacity planning workshop w/ SE 2026-03-04):
- Primary workload: short-chat + embeddings for incident triage; average request ~60 tokens; peak 1.2M tokens/min across system.
- Target latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 700ms for chat generation with model family Llama-3-70B-quantized equivalent.
- Throughput guarantee desired: baseline sustained 500 requests/s (small payloads) per region; burst headroom 40% regionally for attack-day spikes.
- Multi-region plan: initial reserved pools in us-east-1 and eu-west-1; planned us-west-2 cold standby for cost optimization and disaster recovery.
- Per-region sizing proposal from Redwood SE: us-east-1 = 12 reserved GPUs, eu-west-1 = 8 reserved GPUs, us-west-2 standby = 4 reserved GPUs (can be kept as lower-cost reserved or burstable).
- AZ distribution: each regional pool to be spread across at least 2 AZs (50/50 split target) to meet AZ-failure headroom policy.
- Failover headroom: maintain ~20-25% spare capacity in-region for AZ failover and ~15-20% cross-region re-routing capacity.
- Networking: strict egress budgeting requested; need VPC peering diagram and egress estimate attached to SOW.

SLA / commercial asks (negotiation points):
- 99.9% regional availability SLA for reserved pools; credits tied to recognized degraded capacity (not just control plane).
- Clear definition of "throughput guarantee" in tokens/sec and p95 latency bands for each model variant.
- Runbook for automatic failover and cold-start warming; prefer optional warm-burst capacity.
- Penetration of KMS/HSM options and audit log retention 12+ months.
